text:
jia: FYI observed a 95th+ latency uplift on the canary after the kernel-autoselect roll; looks correlated with microburst traffic patterns and KV cache churn. digging in now.

sam: ugh. numbers?

jia: p95 went from 48ms -> 230ms on the canary for small prompt steady-state (seq len ~64). p99 spikes hit ~600ms. logs show lots of kernel switches and KV thrash around request bursts.

alex: do we have a flamegraph / perf profile?

jia: attaching quick perf snapshot from the canary run (trimmed):
```
- 45% time in kernel selection loop
- 30% stalled on kv-store locks (misses + eviction callbacks)
- 15% in attention kernels (switch overhead)
- tail accounted for microbatch assembly + extra coalesce delay jitter under burst
```

maya: sounds like coalesce/jitter interaction with queue policy. when lots of arrivals, the micro-batcher holds a bit longer -> larger batches but kernel selector keeps flipping to larger-kernel paths which are slower for small token budgets.

ben: summary: kernel-autoselect prefers fused kernels when batch_size > B, but our token_budget gating allowed big effective batch size during microbursts. fused kernels have worse latency for many short requests.

sam: so fix options: 1) change threshold B for fused kernels; 2) tweak microbatch interval / jitter to avoid large instantaneous coalesces; 3) adjust token budget target to tighter per-request cap.

alex: also consider adding a short stabilisation-hold after kernel switch so we don't flip on one batch. i.e. hysteresis in kernel selector.

jia: Agreed. I'd like to run an experiment matrix: vary microbatch_interval (0.5ms, 1ms, 2ms), jitter (uniform 0-interval vs gauss 0.5*interval), and token_budget_target (32, 64, 96). keep kernel_threshold B fixed for now, and add a canary with selector hysteresis enabled.

maya: SGTM. small note: microbatch_interval below 1ms increases scheduler wakeups on some HW, watch CPU steal.

perf-bot: deploy-cid: canary-2026-03-17-82 started to eng-runtime/canary-pool at 1710607890

ben: for tracking, add the following config snippet to the experiment so we can reproduce:
```json
{
  "microbatch_interval_ms": 1,
  "coalesce_jitter": "uniform",
  "jitter_scale": 0.5,
  "token_budget_target": 64,
  "kernel_selector_hysteresis_ms": 5
}
```

sam: run 6-hour canaries for each cell and collect p50/95/99 + kernel-switch count + kv-miss rate. also capture cpu steal and scheduler wake metrics.

alex: if we see kernel-switch count >> baseline, we should try hysteresis=10ms.

jia: started the matrix: 3 intervals x 2 jitter modes x 3 token budgets = 18 runs. canaries queued, will roll one every 20 minutes.

maya: thanks. when you have the first results, post the CSV and a best/worst example trace.

perf-bot: canary-run 1 (int=0.5ms jitter=gauss budget=32) finished at 1710609123: p95=190ms p99=510ms kernel-switches=120 kv-miss-rate=0.32

jia: bad — 0.5ms seems too small, lots of kernel flips.

perf-bot: canary-run 5 (int=1ms jitter=uniform budget=64 hysteresis=5ms) finished: p95=52ms p99=120ms kernel-switches=22 kv-miss-rate=0.08

ben: that's promising. 1ms/uniform/64+hysteresis looks close to baseline with lower kv churn.

sam: any CPU steal or scheduler noise?

perf-bot: run 5 cpu_steal 0.7% (baseline 0.4%). acceptable.

alex: let's also check long tail under higher concurrency (x3 load) before approving.

maya: also check cold-KV fill scenarios (cache cold start) — hysteresis might mask an initial wrong kernel decision. we should pair with a KV priming prefetch for known hot keys.

jia: noted. next step: run the 1ms/uniform/64+hysteresis cell at 3x load + cold-kv prefill vs no-prefill.

perf-bot: scheduled extended test at 1710610000 (3x load, cold/primed).

perf-bot: extended test complete at 1710610123: primed p95=58ms p99=150ms kernel-switches=30 kv-miss-rate=0.12; cold p95=95ms p99=260ms kernel-switches=45 kv-miss-rate=0.28

sam: cold case still rough but much better than original. priming helps.

ben: action items: 1) set default microbatch_interval_ms=1, coalesce_jitter=uniform, jitter_scale=0.5, token_budget_target=64; 2) enable kernel_selector_hysteresis_ms=5 for canary rollout; 3) add optional KV prefetch for hot prefixes during cold-start ramp; 4) schedule follow-up to re-evaluate kernel_threshold B after we stabilize.

alex: +1 on that plan. also create a perf regression alert tuned for kernel-switch surge (threshold: +3x baseline switches in 1m).

maya: I'll draft the rollout PR and include the canary metrics and config.

jia: thanks all. I'll update the runbook with the hysteresis and prefetch notes. leaving this thread open for any regressions. :thumbsup:
